costGuide.title: Mercedes M133 Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting a Mercedes M133 typically takes 12-16 hours at £65/hr (independent specialist rate) - confirm exact labour when comparing quotes, as the AMG-specific turbo plumbing and thermal management components require careful access planning.
paragraphs: The final cost of a Mercedes M133 engine replacement is heavily influenced by the condition of the turbocharger and the history of the timing chain. If turbo failure has caused internal oil contamination or if the timing chain has jumped teeth, a standard reconditioned swap may not suffice, pushing the requirement toward a fully rebuilt unit with upgraded thermal management components. See our full reconditioned engine cost guide for a detailed breakdown of what is included at each price tier.

failures.title: Mercedes M133 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Timing Chain Stretch and Tensioner Wear
items.whatHappens: The M133 operates under extreme thermal and mechanical stress. Over time, the timing chain can stretch and the tensioner can lose hydraulic pressure. This manifests as a distinct metallic rattling noise on cold starts, followed by check engine lights indicating camshaft correlation faults. If ignored, the chain can jump teeth, leading to catastrophic valve-to-piston contact.
items.repairVsReplace: If caught early, replacing the timing chain kit, tensioners, and guides is viable, though it is a labour-intensive job requiring significant front-end strip-down. If internal damage has already occurred, a full Mercedes M133 engine replacement is the only reliable solution.

items.title: Turbocharger Wastegate Rattle and Bearing Wear
items.whatHappens: The single large turbocharger is prone to wastegate actuator wear and linkage rattle, leading to boost pressure faults and underboost complaints. In severe cases, bearing wear allows oil to leak into the intake or exhaust tract, causing blue smoke and accelerated carbon buildup.
items.repairVsReplace: Early wastegate rattle can sometimes be addressed with actuator replacement. However, if bearing wear has led to oil ingestion and internal engine scoring, the turbocharger must be replaced, which can push the requirement toward a fully rebuilt unit to prevent repeat failure.

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the Mercedes M133
variants.intro: The M133.980 engine code is stamped directly onto a machined pad on the engine block, typically located near the oil filter housing or the bell housing. It is also clearly listed on your vehicle's V5C registration document under "Engine Number" and can be decoded from the full VIN. Common Confusion Warning: Owners frequently confuse the M133 with other Mercedes 2.0-litre engines: - M139: The direct 2.0L AMG successor introduced in 2019. While similar in displacement, the M139 features a completely different block architecture, revised turbo sizing, and updated engine management, making it incompatible as a direct swap. - M270 and M274: The standard 2.0L turbocharged engines found in non-AMG models. These lack the M133's forged internals, AMG-specific turbocharger, and high-performance ECU mapping. Fitting an M139, M270, or M274 as a direct replacement will result in severe ECU, wiring loom, and exhaust manifold incompatibilities.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement Mercedes M133 - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used Mercedes M133 is only advisable for lower-mileage host vehicles and *only* if accompanied by documented, stamped service history proving rigorous oil changes (every 5,000-8,000 miles) and no prior complaints of cold-start rattles or boost faults. The risk of inheriting timing chain stretch or turbo bearing wear is unacceptably high without this proof.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: This is the most recommended route for the M133. A proper reconditioned unit will include brand-new timing chain components, a tested or replacement turbocharger, and refreshed thermal management seals, directly addressing the AMG engine's known weak points out of the box.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified if your original M133 suffered a jumped timing chain that damaged the cylinder head, valves, or pistons, or if severe turbo failure caused oil starvation to the crankshaft bearings. A specialist rebuild will machine the block, fit upgraded thermal management components, and ensure all oil galleries are clear.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Sourcing a replacement is only half the job. Our network provides full supply and fit services, ensuring the engine is installed by Mercedes and AMG-specialist technicians with a nationwide warranty backing both the labour and the unit.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: For performance hosts like the W176 A45, C117 CLA45, and X156 GLA45, current UK market values typically sit between £12,000 and £35,000 . With a reconditioned M133 replacement costing from £8,000 (plus £1,040-£1,430 fitting), the repair cost generally represents 20-40% of the vehicle's value, making replacement financially viable for well-maintained examples. However, for sub-£12,000 hosts, we strongly advise evaluating the car's scrap or part-exchange value before committing to an AMG engine replacement.

items.question: Can I swap another engine code in place of M133?
